newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - NOV 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - NOV 22.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI

--The government is considering ways to better ensure incoming revenues from the new taxes announced recently on real estate and state titles. Reports say taxpayers will be asked to submit an exhaustive declaration on their real estate holdings. The government believes that it will not be easy for Greek investors to take advantage of the loophole that exempts foreign purchasers of state titles from the tax, due to double taxation provisions.

--Some 29 brokerage firms go through the exhaustive checks conducted by the Deloitte & Touche, Peat Marwick and Ernst & Young. Under the microscope are all transactions since October 15 to the present today in trading on eight listed firms.

--Budgets for the 48 public utilities and organisations (DEKO) were decided yesterday. The 1997 budget sees all DEKOs with positive economic returns but their wages bills are still overshooting targets.
--The development ministry will meet on Monday to discuss whether to extend the licence for Nafsi to operate as a shipyard.
IMERISIA

--The 'objective evaluation' system for real estate will be extended to 61 municipalities and communities, Deputy Finance Minister George Drys is expected to announce today. The prices in the system will be used to evaluate taxes on the transfer and donation of real estate as well as the new real estate tax.
--The exexmption threshold for the new real estate tax will be set at 150 million drachmas for a four-member family, Drys adds.

--State-run banks are continually losing ground to private sector banks, which indicates a need for state banks to re-evaluate their operating criteria and for shareholders to elect administration and management.
--Ergo Bank has plans to establish a new investment bank in cooperation with a major international bank.
--Unimar Shipping faces bankruptcy as seamen on 12 of the 25 vessels have yet to be paid and 48 staff take over the company building; the owners have dropped out of sight.
KERDOS

--The finance ministry has legal experts searching for possible loopholes in the taxation of state titles and real estate. The new procedures will have to walk a fine line between Greece's obligations under international treaties on double taxation as well as being a water-tight system for collecting the dues.
--The partial privatisation of the Bank of Attica can go ahead, following an agreement between the Commercial Bank and TSEMEDE.
EXPRESS

--Are mutual funds involved in the recent problems at the Athens Stock Exchange? Recent reports from the market allege that at least two mutual fund management companies were involved in specific share transactions.

--The three-year fixed-rate bond makes its grand premiere today as its goes on sale. The finance ministry is confident of a good showing at today's auction, following the return of calm to the interbank market and the fact that tax-exempt state titles will end with the New Year.

--A new code for procurements contracts with the state will be in force as of the beginning of 1997. The code - awaiting signing by the president - attempts to shed as much light as possible on procedures and make them accountable.
NAFTEMBORIKI
--Businessmen call on the government to intervene with local government following dramatic increases in municipal charges, hurting, mainly, local merchants.

--The realisation of the Community Support Framework will be a major juncture for the government's economic policy in 1997:inflows from the EU are expected to reach 700 billion drachmas next year, up 100 billion. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
